title: has one part per row
why: A part whose row was renamed in the walkthrough would go unwalked with nothing said.

find: table: 'Revert, while a chosen day is not drawn',
title: puts each part
why: A part whose result names no table row would be written nowhere, or into the wrong cell.

replace: words: ['A feed is a timetable of the transit agency.'],
title: types no sentence
why: A sentence typed into a script is heard against itself, not against the app.

title: compares letters and digits only
why: Without whole-word matching, unchecked would be heard as checked.

title: appends to a cell
why: A script that overwrites a cell erases a person's word.

title: keeps the clause in one cell
why: A semicolon in a phrase would end the clause early and the record test would read a stray one.

title: never writes pass
why: A row whose script stopped would be written as heard.

title: never writes pass
why: A script that listened for nothing would be written as heard.

title: refuses a role
why: A role with no words in the synonyms table would be wanted as nothing, and heard.

title: reads the walkthrough
why: A bold name broken over two lines would be lost, and its row unwalked.

title: does not hear checked or pressed
why: "on" would be heard as a toggle pressed, which VoiceOver also says of a switch that is on.

title: does not hear checked or pressed
why: "not checked" would be heard as checked.

title: does not take a role or a state word
why: A role word inside a control's name would stand for its role.

title: refuses to want nothing
why: An empty text is found in anything, so a row wanting it is heard whatever was said.

title: refuses to want nothing
why: A control with no name would be heard by its role word alone.

title: does not credit an action
why: The tail of the phrase before an action, reported again by Guidepup, would be credited to the action.

title: writes no path into a clause
why: A machine's folder path would be written into the public record.

title: types no word into what a row is to hear
why: A word typed into a walk is heard against itself, not against the app.

title: types no word into what a row is to hear
why: A word typed into what a press is to be heard with is heard against itself.
